 On Friday, Konyaspor will face Galatasaray in Turkey, Le Havre and PSG will battle in France, while Lille and Lens will lock horns later in the day. Below are analyses and odds for these games.
 Claim Your Registration Bonus! Konyaspor vs Galatasaray
 Konyaspor have not been consistent since the start of the new season, despite recording a 2-0 win over Genclerbirligi in their last game, with Chidozie Awaziem getting a brace. The Anatolian Eagles have managed to claim just eight points in the opening nine games of the season, and they are closer to the relegation zone than to the top of the table. Facing the league leader in this game sends another type of challenge. Meanwhile, Galatasaray secured a 2-1 win over Fenerbahçe in their last game in the Istanbul derby to move to the top of the table with 22 points in nine games. Gala have been on fire since getting back from the international break with four wins in five games in all competitions, with the only loss coming against Barcelona. So, as things stand, I see them getting another win in this game, but I doubt if they can keep a clean sheet.

 Le Havre vs PSG
 Le Havre suffered a 4-3 loss to Marseille in their last game, going 4-0 down before pulling three back. Substitute Josh Maja could only do less, with a brace, in the fight for a comeback. People have started to compare their form to last season, where they collected 35 points, and early indicators have suggested they might not pick up to those points this season. This season, they sit at the bottom of the table with zero wins, including two draws. Meanwhile, after a challenging start to the season, PSG have now won their last eight games in all competitions. They beat Lyon in their last game to move to the top of the table and have now won each of their last five games in the league. They have been equally impressive on the continent, where they have 100% win record in the three games in the UEFA Champions League. This includes wins over Manchester City and Barcelona.

 Lille vs Lens
 Lille have been impressive since the start of the season, going unbeaten in all but one game. Their only loss came in a 2-1 loss to Nice on the road. At home, their unbeaten run remains intact in the league. In their last game, they played a one-all draw against Monaco, despite playing with ten men for almost 30 minutes of the game. At the moment, they sit third on the table with two points off the league’s top. Meanwhile, Lens have seen four wins, one draw, and three defeats this season, but their inconsistency could be the defining factor in this game. They secured a 2-1 win in their last game against Paris FC, extending their winning run to three straight games in the league. However, their away form has been poor, remaining winless in three of their four games on the road.
